### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, touching **204** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/package.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**82** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/mcp/package.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `recordId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (symbol, 39 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **38** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **40** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee710cd65cc853bddc416be86b6722e6ec0b3eb1` — the merge of head `da6a24cb0dbd72ce3f4841c7709bf332ed8975ef` into base `24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee710cd65cc853bddc416be86b6722e6ec0b3eb1 && git checkout ee710cd65cc853bddc416be86b6722e6ec0b3eb1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821 da6a24cb0dbd72ce3f4841c7709bf332ed8975ef && git checkout -B drift-repro 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821 && git merge --no-ff da6a24cb0dbd72ce3f4841c7709bf332ed8975ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 24bc259363f11c384a5d6ade8da9d497a2c77821` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `67847d9c089ce3e923d9102b042916a824e548f3`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the widening face and its security face — `packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.ts` (new, the verbs and the link door), `storage-routes.ts` (the two `upload-links` routes, `mintDownloadUrl`, `DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_TTL`, the filename and media-type readers, `relayUploadLinkRefusal`), `metadata-store.ts` (`updateFileIfUnchanged`), `upload-link-page.ts`, `upload-link-wire.ts`, `storage-route-ledger.ts`, `storage-service-plugin.ts` (`bindRecordFileAccess`, `resolveUploadLinkDoor`), `file-attachment-service.ts` (the five delegating verbs); `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` (`registerFileTools`), `file-content.ts` (new), `skill-md.ts`, `package.json` (`unpdf` 1.9.1); `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` (`resolveMcpRecordFileService`, `recordFileMembers`, `publicOrigin`, `absoluteUrl`); the five suites (`record-file-access.integration.test.ts` 21, `mcp-file-tools.test.ts` 21, `mcp-record-file-bridge.test.ts` 5, `showcase-mcp-record-files.dogfood.test.ts`, the route-count, ledger, unknown-argument and skill-surface pins, the `authz-conformance` GATE_PIN regex); `.changeset/30892-mcp-read-file-upload-link.md` (the ② input); the prose faces `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`, `plugin-endpoints.mdx`, `system-context.mdx` row 47e, the tenant-audit census and its counts ledger; `pnpm-lock.yaml` (three `unpdf` hunks) + cited on `origin/main`: `storage-routes.ts` 700–760 (`refuseHeldSession`, `mountFamilyRoute`, the ADR-0069 gate), 298–380 (`StorageUploadSession`, `resolveSession`), 2009 (`buildKey`); `storage-service-plugin.ts` 1149–1227 (`composeStorageRoutes`: the one place `resolveSession` is wired, `buildAuthSessionResolver`); `metadata-store.ts` 125–160 (`StorageWriteContext`, `writeOptionsFor`, `systemByIdWriteOptionsFor`), 519–600 (`getFile` system by-id read, `updateFile`, `deleteFile`); `attachment-access-hooks.ts` 405–470 (`mayEditAttachmentParent`, `parentUpdateAdmits`, the degraded read); `file-attachment-service.ts` 224–260 (`assertMayAttach`); `objects/system-file.object.ts` 55–72, 118–126, 196–200, 266–270 (which `sys_file` columns are `readonly`: the storage-owned five, the reference columns and `owner_id`; `name` and `metadata` are not); `sys-file-storage-owned-columns.ts` header (the create-side stamp of `owner_id`); `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` and `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (every code the diff throws); `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts` 325 (`isFileIdToken`); `packages/qa/dogfood/test/anonymous-door-sweep.classification.ts` 148–182 (a token-addressed route not in a door class is everything-else and must answer 401); `docs/adr/0138-…md` D2; `packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts` 488 (`allowCredentials` default false); AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 and `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md` 313 (the declaration lines and when `Skills-docs:` is owed).

Inputs read: card #30892 body and all seven comments (triage 6685125943, seat 4's two claims 6685222837 / 6685332126, the progress ping 6689332927, seat 4's brief 6690566522, the ruling 6691366983, the dev's current os-dev report 6691432611 on head `67847d9c`, which supersedes 6690647935); PR #31009's body, its 30-file list (3947+ / 86−), its eight commits over merge-base `8ae0ab9b` (`75bc8cfa` the feature, `ebd0dbc4`, `e3f0aa4e`, `bc5ad15b`, `04ff76bc` option B, `c5fe7df9` the `main` merge, `f30868c7` and `67847d9c` test-only CI fixes); the one PR comment, the docs-drift bot 6690667667; the net diff `origin/main...67847d9c`; the check-runs on `67847d9c`, read at 2026-11-06T17:58Z: 66 total, 59 `completed/success`, 7 `completed/skipped` (opt-in and matrix placeholders: `UI Published Artifacts`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Schedule gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the matrix-shard placeholder, `18.x upgrade harness`), 0 failed, 0 in progress (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates` with every `Lint ·` leg, `Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / source gates / debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` 1–8 and aggregate, `Test UI` 1–16 and aggregate, `Live E2E UI`, `Validate Package Dependencies`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check PR Size`). Both carriers read by eye: PR body and changeset each carry `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as line-initial keys, one each. The PR is a draft, `mergeable: true`, author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, branch `claude/project-thread-s2vcdk`, `Fixes #30892`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Token entropy.** The link is `UUID.SECRET`: the UUID is the row id (`randomUUID`), the secret is `randomBytes(32)` in base64url — 256 bits, 43 characters without padding. `parseToken` shape-checks both halves (`LINK_ID`, `LINK_SECRET`) before any read, so a malformed token never reaches the store. Pinned (`grant.token` matches the two-part shape). TRUE.
- **Hashed at rest.** The row's `metadata` holds `secret_sha256` only (`sha256Hex(secret)`); the secret is in the mint answer and nowhere else — not in the row, not in a log line, not in the page. The compare is `sameDigest`: equal-length hex buffers under `timingSafeEqual`. Pinned (the row's `metadata` does not contain the secret). TRUE.
- **Single use.** The spend is one compare-and-set: `updateFileIfUnchanged(store, id, { status: 'pending', name: 'upload-link' }, { name: 'upload-link (used)' })` — `engine.update` on `sys_file` with `where: { id, status, name }` and `multi: true`, answering the matched-row count, with a thrown fault when the count is not a number so an unknown outcome is never read as either; the spend counts only when the matched count is above zero. The engine-absent stand-in is one synchronous Map compare-and-set. The guard columns are `status` and `name` because a JSON `metadata` string cannot be a `where` value (the engine reads a `{…}`-shaped string as a filter placeholder) — the reason is written at the guard type. After the write chain, `finally` deletes the row; a failed delete leaves a row named used, which `openLinkStateOf` refuses on `name`. Pinned: second use `404`, the used link's page `404`, the race (two concurrent uses: `[200, 404]`) in both the package suite and the dogfood; the dev's ablation (`if (!spent)` flipped) turned the race pin red. TRUE.
- **Expiry.** `expires_at` = mint + 600 s, checked in `openLink` on both the page and the upload (a deadline at or before now is refused, as is a non-finite one). `UPLOAD_LINK_TTL_SECONDS` is exported and the pins read it. Pinned in both suites by moving `Date.now` past the TTL (page and PUT `404`, nothing lands); the dev's ablation (the deadline check removed) turned the expiry pin red. An expired, never-used row stays `pending` for the pending-upload retention (`attachment-lifecycle.ts`, 7 days), stated in the body. TRUE.
- **One same-shaped answer, so the answer is not an oracle.** Every refusal inside `openLink` — a token that is not one, no row, a row that is not an open link (used, not pending, not a link, unparsable metadata, a missing binding field), a digest mismatch, expiry, a session naming another user — is `refuseUnusableLink()`: `404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` with the one sentence in `upload-link-wire.ts`. The routes map it to the one page (`sendUnusableUploadLinkPage`) on GET and the one JSON envelope on PUT; a kernel without the door answers the same two. The signed-out caller is a different shape, `401 AUTH_REQUIRED`, and that is correct rather than an oracle: `uploadLinkCaller` runs before the token is read at all, so a signed-out request gets `401` for any token — valid, used, expired, unknown or malformed alike — and learns nothing about it; it is the answer ADR-0138 D2's everything-else class requires. Pinned: the package suite's one loop over the used, forged, unknown and malformed tokens (PUT and page), the other-user case for two users, the expired case; the dogfood's used, unknown and admin-as-stranger cases. TRUE.
- **Never acts without sign-in (ruling B).** Both routes are mounted through `mountFamilyRoute` (the ADR-0069 held-session gate first) and call `uploadLinkCaller` before anything else: it reads `opts.resolveSession` — the one `buildAuthSessionResolver` wired in `composeStorageRoutes` — and sends `401` when there is no session, no resolver (fails closed, unlike the bare-kernel upload doors) or a resolver that throws. The user it answers is the request's own session user, handed to `inspectUploadLink` / `consumeUploadLink` as `callerUserId`, and `openLink` refuses when `state.user_id` differs. No branch mints, opens or spends on the token alone. The page's script `PUT`s to `location.pathname` with `credentials: 'same-origin'`, so the browser's session rides along. Pinned: no session `401` on page and PUT with the link still open afterwards (package suite and dogfood, the latter over the real `/api/v1/storage/upload-links/:token` with Bearer sessions); another signed-in user `404`, not spent. Nothing in the diff contradicts ruling B: the tool description, the skill lines, the ledger notes, `connect-mcp.mdx` and the changeset all say the link works only for its user, signed in. The one place A survives is prose (should-fix 2). TRUE.
- **Organization boundary.** At mint the row is stamped with the caller's `tenantId` (`createFile(..., { organizationId })`) and the binding carries `organization_id`. At use the row is read by id under the store's system by-id read (unscoped, as every `getFile` is), then the user must match; the spend and the delete run under `writeContext = { organizationId }` from the binding (`systemByIdWriteOptionsFor` scopes the statement by it), and the user is re-resolved in that organization: `resolveUserAuthzGrants` with `bypassGrantsCache` and `vetOrganizationClaim` under the admission posture — an unbacked claim answers `null` and the upload is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` before the spend. The field write is `engine.update` as that user (RLS, field security, hooks), the attachment write is `attachFileAs` as that user with the binding's `organizationId`. A user signed in to another organization than the link's still acts, for this upload, in the organization the link was minted in, as its grants there allow — the right reading, since the record lives there. Pinned: revoked reach `403` with nothing landed and no stray `sys_file`; the dogfood runs under the showcase's owner RLS and `controlled_by_parent`. TRUE.
- **Binding.** `record_id`, `field` / `attachments` and `user_id` come from the row alone; the PUT reads no query parameter and only two headers (`x-file-name`, `content-type`), both sanitised (`uploadLinkFilename`: last path segment, control characters dropped, 255 chars, `.`/`..` refused; `uploadLinkMimeType`: a media type or `application/octet-stream`). Pinned in both suites with a request naming another record, field and user in headers and query string. TRUE.
- **Access follows the record.** `readRecordAs` reads as the caller with raw file values and maps a refused or missing row to `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` with `get_record`'s sentence; the bridge reads through `callData('get')` first, so an unreadable record is refused before storage is asked (bridge pin and dogfood pin: `read.code === door.code`). A field file is the id the caller's own read returns (field-level security decides), an attachment is a caller-scoped `sys_attachment` read bound to that record (an attachment of another record `404`). The file itself takes the download door's own verdict (`judgeFileRead`, bound by the plugin, `public_read` short-circuit as the door has) and answers that door's `403` codes. Mint asks `assertMayAttach` (attachments) or `mayEditAttachmentParent` + `getWritableFields` (field). TRUE.
- **Refusal codes and messages.** `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` 404, `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` 404, `FILE_NOT_FOUND` 404, `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400, `INVALID_REQUEST` 400, `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403, `FIELD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` 403, `ATTACHMENT_DOWNLOAD_DENIED` 403, `FILE_DOWNLOAD_DENIED` 403, `AUTH_REQUIRED` 401, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` 413, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` 503 — every one is in `errors.zod.ts` or the error-code ledger; `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` (pinned at mint) is the attach door's own. `relayUploadLinkRefusal` relays a 4xx with its code and message and the two declared 5xx outages only, so a fault's text never reaches the link holder. No runtime string carries a tracker number (`check:doc-authoring` green). The MCP side renders refusals through `errorResultWithCode` (ADR-0112 envelope; pinned on `read_file` and `create_upload_link`). TRUE.
- **The page.** CSP `default-src 'none'` with per-response nonces for the inline script and style, `connect-src 'self'`, `form-action 'none'`, `frame-ancestors 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`; `no-store`, `no-referrer`, `noindex`, `nosniff`, `DENY`. It names the target kind and the expiry only. Pinned (headers; the HTML contains neither the record id, the object name nor the user). A cross-site PUT with the session cookie needs a CORS preflight that allows credentials, and `allowCredentials` defaults false. TRUE.
- **Tests pin each refusal; ablations where the body claims them.** The package suite's 21 cover the read cap, record access on read and mint (`404` / `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` / `403 ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS`), the system context (`403`), the non-file field, multi-file naming, the page headers, the binding, single use with one same-shaped `404` for four token states, no session `401` not spent, another user `404` not spent, the race, expiry, `413` before the spend (bytes and declared length), revoked reach `403` with nothing landed, `maxSize` refused with the bytes removed. The MCP suite's 21 cover registration by scope, argument refusals, the `sys_*` refusal, relayed codes, the cap, image, PDF, damaged PDF, docx, docx bomb, unknown type, skill lines by scope. The bridge's 5 cover the `get_record` door first, the principal, absolute links, no members without the seam. The dogfood runs the composed chain. The body claims two ablations (spend guard, expiry) and reports both red; they are the dev's readings (`Local-runs: none`), consistent with what the pins assert. TRUE.
- **PR body vs diff.** Every claim in "What changes" and "The upload-link security surface" is in the diff; the figures (10 MiB / 100 000 chars / 200 pages / 32 MiB / 5 MiB, 600 s, 300 s, 32 bytes) match the constants; `unpdf` pinned exactly, loaded by dynamic import with `isEvalSupported: false`, `disableFontFace`, `useSystemFonts: false`; docx by `inflateRawSync` with `maxOutputLength`. The two routes are ledgered `server-only`, the mount count moves 10 to 12 and the pins say so. TRUE.

### ② Semver level

Both carriers read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial, one each. `widening` is right: two tools join the MCP surface where the storage service is installed, two signed-in routes join the storage family, and nothing that answered before answers differently (the two download doors now mint through `mintDownloadUrl`, same URL). `none` is right: no spec file, no key, no object (the link is a pending `sys_file` row, D2). No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (`none` with a `(widening)` arm). The level follows the rule: a non-protocol widening ships `patch` — `patch` on `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-storage`, the three published packages the diff moves. No BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker owed. `Check Changeset` green on this head.

Check-runs on `67847d9c`: 59 success / 7 skipped / 0 failed / 0 in progress (list above). Draft; no governed surface in the file list (no `docs/adr/**`, no `packages/spec/**`), the brief expects not-governed and asks the seat to re-run `check-governed-merges` on the final list.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in 6691432611: one, the A/B sign-in choice. Answered by ruling 6691366983: B, as built. Nothing else is open.
- Out-of-scope notes of the dev, read: `dispatch-gates --commands` does not derive the dogfood's `typecheck` (CI's `Type Check · workspace` caught it, fixed `f30868c7`) — a tooling card, not this PR's; the ADR-0069 hold on the minting user is not re-checked at use (the uploading request's own session is gated by `mountFamilyRoute`, and the minting user is the uploading user under B, so the hold is checked on the request that matters); the link path follows the plugin `basePath`; no byte quota in the open tree (cloud's half). All stand as filed.
- File surface: inside seat 4's claim except the seven the body lists (`packages/mcp/package.json` + lockfile for D1, `plugin-endpoints.mdx`, the two census pages and the counts ledger, gate-forced, the parity dogfood's comment); `packages/runtime/src/mcp-record-file-bridge.test.ts` is the runtime half's test, which the claim allows. No `packages/spec/**`, `ui/**`, `skills/**`.
- Inside `service-storage`, beyond calling existing doors, the diff adds the two routes, the page, the wire module and the conditional update — the "one single-use upload-link record" the claim allows, plus the doors that serve it; the record is a `sys_file` row, so no new object.
- The docs-drift bot (6690667667) lists 81 hand-written docs naming a touched symbol; the three pages the diff edits are the ones the surface change makes stale, and `plugin-endpoints.mdx` carries the two routes. The lane seat's ACCEPT reads the rest.
- security#1: the security face is covered here at rule level; should-fix 1 is a hardening with a one-line fix. Recommend a notice to security#1 on landing (a new token-bearing route pair), not a hold.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; `Fixes #30892`; the merge of `main` at `c5fe7df9` (not rebased, stated) brings #30861's `mcp-http-tools.ts` beside this diff with no conflict.
- Independence: rendered by an isolated contract-review subagent fed the card and its comments, the ruling, the brief, the PR body, the os-dev report, the net diff, the cited code on `origin/main`, the error-code ledger, the sweep classification and the check-runs — not the seat's or the dev's conclusions; adopted by the seat named in `Reviewed-by:`.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The widening against the MCP contract.** Two tools, each registered only where the bridge carries its member and under its scope family, both refusing `sys_*` as the object tools do, both judged by existing doors (`get_record`'s read, the download door's verdict, the attach rule, the record's own update) — the diff adds no second access judgment, which the module doc states and the code holds. The four-axis reading: declared ⇒ enforced holds (each refusal the body lists is a pinned code); tightening over leniency holds (the link doors fail closed with no resolver, the spend is all-or-nothing, a refused write after the spend discards bytes and row). Holds.
- **Option B's shape.** Binding the token to a session makes the token a second factor rather than a capability: a leaked or forwarded link opens nothing for anyone else, and the anonymous-door sweep's everything-else class holds with no ADR-0138 amendment. The cost the body states (sign in on the phone first) is the ruling's. The upload acting as the minting user with grants re-resolved (D3) is the right side of the signed-URL precedent: no write runs as the system on a user's behalf. Holds.
- **`record-file-access.ts`.** The order of `consumeUploadLink` — open, validate, size gate, re-resolve, spend, write, delete — puts every refusal that should not cost the link ahead of the spend and every refusal that must cost it after; the body's "strict single use" paragraph matches it. `openLink` is one function for both routes so the page and the upload can never disagree on what a usable link is. The state-in-`name` choice is forced by the engine's placeholder reading of a `{…}` string and is written at the guard; it has one consequence the diff does not close (should-fix 1). Holds.
- **`storage-routes.ts` and the plugin.** The doors read nothing but the token, the session, the body and two sanitised headers; the service verbs are reached through the kernel's `file-attachments` service per request so a host mount and the plugin's serve the same links; `bindRecordFileAccess` binds the download verdict, servability, the user re-resolution and the TTL from the kernel, in the one place the other gates are bound. Holds.
- **The pins.** The matrix per refusal × door, the race, the two ablations, the composed dogfood over real sessions and RLS. Holds.

Findings (none must-fix):

1. **should-fix (hardening)** — `packages/services/service-storage/src/record-file-access.ts`, `openLink`: the link's state (`name`) and binding (`metadata`) live in two `sys_file` columns that are not `readonly` (`objects/system-file.object.ts`), and `sys_file` carries no owner rule, so a caller holding a `sys_file` edit grant can rewrite a pending link row's binding or user through the data door; the readonly, system-stamped `owner_id` on the same row already names the minting user. Rule: a link is usable only when the binding's user is the row's stamped uploader — add `row.owner_id === state.user_id` to `openLink`'s checks (one line, the same `refuseUnusableLink` answer) and pin it; state in the module doc that the binding's other columns rest on `sys_file` edit being an administrative grant. Not must-fix: the upload still runs as the bound user under every gate, the grant is administrative, and the row is deleted after use.
